ai.description: The Himalayan Pit-viper reaches 50–70 cm. It is grey-brown with dark, irregular dorsal blotches and a distinct, pale post-ocular stripe. It features a triangular head and heat-sensing loreal pits.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Gloydius himalayanus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark post-ocular stripe that extends behind the eye, contrasting with its pale labials.
ai.habitat: The Himalayan Pit-viper inhabits rocky, mountainous terrain and coniferous forests across the Himalayas, typically at elevations ranging from 1,500 to 3,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Himalayan pit-viper is primarily nocturnal, often remaining motionless for extended periods to ambush small prey like rodents and lizards along rocky mountain slopes.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gloydius himalayanus* is ovoviviparous, typically producing a small litter of 3–6 young. Mating occurs in late spring, with births recorded during late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Himalayan Pit-viper is found in the high-altitude regions of the Indian Himalayas, specifically in Himachal Pradesh and Ladakh, at elevations above 3,000 meters.
